source.title: Counterbalancing Teacher: Regularizing Batch Normalized Models for Robustness
source.authors: Saeid Asgari Taghanaki; A. Gholami; Fereshte Khani; Kristy Choi; Linh-Tam Tran; Ran Zhang; A. Khani

record.file_problem: Full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests how normalization affects training outcomes and robustness, and reports a synthetic MNIST comparison where a BN model fails when its learned low-variance features are removed. Its results do not test the claim versions about training error, width, depth, initialization, learning-rate stability, or training speed.
record.gate_note: Results on clean and shifted accuracy, corruption error, domain generalization, and predictive uncertainty bear on the broader claim about normalization and model outcomes. The paper does not report training classification error or test the claim versions' stated outcomes. Cited claims about BN accelerating convergence are prior work, not results of this study.
record.test_reason: The paper cites BN's convergence benefits but does not test any listed version. Its own results concern feature reliance, test accuracy, corruption robustness and calibration, rather than training error, optimization speed, trainable depth, local minima or learning-rate stability. Robustness costs do not qualify V6, which makes no robustness guarantee.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors argue that normalization encourages reliance on predictive low-variance features, supported by linear-model analysis and robustness experiments. They propose CT, using a trained, frozen unnormalized teacher to regularize a BN student, and report improved robustness and generalization. They acknowledge the additional teacher-training cost; inference uses only the student.
record.recipe_differences: The study concerns normalization's effect on robustness and a teacher-student regularizer, not the claim versions' training-error, width, depth, initialization, learning-rate, or training-speed experiments. It evaluates shifted accuracy and corruption error rather than training classification error.
record.method_sensitivity: Normalization choice (BN, LN, IN, or none), dataset and shift type, and test-time BN adaptation corruption and batch size affect reported outcomes.

fits_no_version.finding: In synthetic MNIST, removing both colored-square cues causes the BN classifier to fail substantially while the no-BN classifier retains high accuracy; exact accuracies are not readable from the supplied text.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: BN can encourage reliance on predictive low-variance cues, reducing test accuracy when those cues disappear.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 5.2 reports lower corruption errors without normalization than with BN, LN or IN, and approximately 4% and 3% improvements with CT for WideResNet and ResNext.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Normalization choice and CT regularization affect corruption robustness.

fits_no_version.finding: CT improves corruption error over most listed augmentation baselines; on CIFAR-10-C WideResNet, its 11.6 mCE is slightly higher than AugMix's 11.2.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: CT can improve corruption robustness, with gains depending on architecture and comparator.

fits_no_version.finding: CT reports improved average domain generalization and point-cloud accuracy, lower ImageNet-C error and a smaller background gap. Point-cloud gains vary by shift, with Rotation and Occlusion worsening.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: CT can improve performance under distribution shift, but improvements are condition dependent.

fits_no_version.finding: Removing BN improves PointNet accuracy on Noise and Sparse but lowers it on other listed conditions; DenseNet without BN has a higher mean Camelyon-17 test accuracy with overlapping reported uncertainty.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Removing BN has mixed effects on OOD test performance across datasets and shifts.

record.problems: The synthetic MNIST accuracy comparisons are figure-only without stated numbers. Several headline comparisons are figure-only; the text does not provide exact values. Some reported domain generalization and point-cloud comparisons include few summary statistics, and uncertainty is absent for several tables.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-version result rows were omitted. Table 4 uncertainty metrics and detailed adaptation comparisons in Figure 4 and Table 8 concern predictive calibration or test-time BN adaptation rather than the versions' named training outcomes; Figure 2(b) varies CT regularization strength and does not measure a listed version.

untested.parts: Training classification error of randomly initialized CNNs on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, including random or corrupted labels and effects of model size, stopping and regularization.
Spurious local minima in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems and the effect of extra student neurons. CT's teacher-student framework addresses a different question.
Training-error degradation with depth, identity-shortcut controls, deep plain tanh initialization and normalization-free residual training.
Effects of activation-matched, Gaussian or orthogonal initialization on training speed, signal propagation and trainable depth.
Loss and curvature trajectories relative to learning-rate stability thresholds, recovery, divergence and edge-of-stability behavior.
Matched BN versus no-BN accuracy trajectories, higher-learning-rate tolerance and Fixup's training speed and stability.

record.verdict_notes: All row states are cannot_determine with respect to V1–V6 because their measures cannot establish those versions, even where robustness values are numerical. CT performance rows should remain separate from claim-version evidence. No omitted result in the supplied text tests a listed version; predictive sharpness in Table 4 is not loss-Hessian sharpness in V5.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error from random initialization on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, and effects of size, early stopping, or regularization.
Teacher-student ReLU width sweeps and spurious local minima.
Depth comparisons with and without identity shortcuts; special initialization and normalization-free residual training.
Activation-matched or orthogonal initialization effects on learning speed and trainable depth.
Training above stability thresholds, loss and curvature trajectories, and sharpness behavior.
Whether BN speeds accuracy gains or permits higher learning rates, and whether Fixup matches normalized residual training.

rows.subject: network trained with batch normalization
rows.size_stated: small CNN; architecture specified in Table 5
rows.operation_detail: Trained on synthetic MNIST binary classification with red and blue square cues, then evaluated on the None test set with neither square.

conditions.value: SGD, TensorFlow default parameters, batch size 128, 100 epochs, no augmentation

rows.measure: Classification accuracy on the None test set
rows.note: Text says the BN model drastically fails when the colored-square features are missing, but gives no numerical accuracy.
rows.check: Missing-cue test accuracy cannot establish any listed optimization effect. Exact accuracy is unavailable in the supplied figure extraction.

rows.subject: network without normalization (NoBN)
rows.size_stated: small CNN; architecture specified in Table 5 with BN layers omitted
rows.operation_detail: Trained on synthetic MNIST binary classification with red and blue square cues, then evaluated on the None test set with neither square.

conditions.value: SGD, TensorFlow default parameters, batch size 128, 100 epochs, no augmentation

rows.measure: Classification accuracy on the None test set
rows.note: The text says NoBN does not drastically fail when the square features are missing, but provides no numeric accuracy.
rows.check: High missing-cue test accuracy does not measure any listed version; observed is therefore inappropriate.

rows.subject: WideResNet 40-2 with no normalization (NN)
rows.operation_detail: Compared clean-trained models with no normalization, batch normalization, layer normalization, or instance normalization on corrupted CIFAR-10-C inputs.
rows.note: Authors state the no-normalization model outperforms all three normalization types on corrupted data; plotted values are not stated in text.
rows.check: Corruption error measures robustness, not a listed optimization effect.

rows.subject: ResNext
rows.operation_detail: Compared clean-trained models with no normalization and normalization on corrupted CIFAR-10-C inputs.
rows.note: Figure caption says CT achieves lower corruption errors than normalizing methods for both ResNext and WideResNet; precise per-model comparison of NN is not stated in text.
rows.check: Corruption error measures robustness. Section 5.2 describes NN outperforming normalization variants across Figure 3, but exact ResNext values cannot be recovered from the supplied text.

rows.subject: WideResNet with CT
rows.operation_detail: Trained a BN student regularized by a frozen, unnormalized teacher; compared with normalized models on CIFAR-10-C.
rows.note: Paper reports corruption errors improve significantly with CT.
rows.check: The study's proposed method's corruption-error improvement is not a claim-version result. The approximately 4% improvement is reported without an explicitly identified numerical baseline.

rows.subject: ResNext with CT
rows.operation_detail: Trained a BN student regularized by a frozen, unnormalized teacher; compared with normalized models on CIFAR-10-C.
rows.note: Paper reports corruption errors improve significantly with CT.
rows.check: The study's proposed method's corruption-error improvement is not a claim-version result. The approximately 3% improvement is reported without an explicitly identified numerical baseline.

rows.note: CT reported as outperforming six of seven methods and comparable to AugMix.
rows.check: This is the study's method compared with robustness baselines, not an optimization result. Table 1 CT uses random individual AutoAugment operations; this condition should be recorded.

rows.subject: ResNet-18 with CT
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated domain generalization accuracy on VLCS with each domain partitioned into train and test sets.

conditions.value: four domains; averaged over three runs

rows.note: CT outperforms the state of the art on 3 out of 4 domains and by 1.83% on average, per the text.
rows.check: Domain generalization accuracy is the study's method performance, not an optimization measure. The omitted comparison is Shape Bias: average 75.79 versus CT 77.60; CT is lower on Pascal, 74.10 versus 74.33.

rows.subject: PointNet-CT
rows.operation_detail: Trained with CT on clean original point-cloud data and evaluated on six shifted test sets.

conditions.value: Original, Noise, Translation, MissingPart, Sparse, Rotation, Occlusion

rows.baseline: PointNet: Original 89.06; Noise 74.72; Translation 79.66; MissingPart 81.52; Sparse 60.53; Rotation 8.83; Occlusion 39.47; Avg. 61.97
rows.value: Original 89.83; Noise 78.12; Translation 82.25; MissingPart 82.58; Sparse 68.40; Rotation 7.62; Occlusion 38.10; Avg. 63.84
rows.note: CT improves several shifts and average accuracy; accuracy is lower than PointNet on Sparse? No, higher there, but lower on Rotation and Occlusion.
rows.check: Shifted test accuracy does not measure a listed version. CT improves Original and four shifts but lowers Rotation and Occlusion accuracy; these mixed robustness results are not a partial optimization effect.

rows.subject: PointNet-noBN
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated the model without BN on clean original and six shifted point-cloud test sets.
rows.baseline: PointNet: Original 89.06; Noise 74.72; Translation 79.66; MissingPart 81.52; Sparse 60.53; Rotation 8.83; Occlusion 39.47
rows.value: Original 87.99; Noise 78.65; Translation 79.02; MissingPart 76.82; Sparse 72.61; Rotation 6.89; Occlusion 35.13
rows.note: NoBN improves Noise and Sparse but is lower on Original, Translation, MissingPart, Rotation, and Occlusion.
rows.check: Removing BN is evaluated for test robustness, not training speed or learning-rate tolerance. Table 3 also reports average accuracy 62.44 versus baseline 61.97.

rows.subject: ResNet-50 with CT
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated mean corruption error on ImageNet-C after training on original images.
rows.check: This is preliminary performance of the study's method on corrupted validation images, not a listed optimization result.

rows.subject: DenseNet-121 without BN
rows.note: NoBN is higher than the BN baseline, but CT is reported as highest.
rows.check: OOD test accuracy cannot establish BN's training-speed effect. The reported uncertainties also do not establish a statistically reliable improvement.

rows.subject: DenseNet-121 with CT
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated CT test accuracy on Camelyon-17.
rows.note: Paper reports CT gets the best test accuracy.
rows.check: This is the study's method's OOD test performance, not a listed optimization result; the highest reported mean alone does not establish statistical significance.

rows.subject: ResNet-50 with CT
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated accuracy on ImageNet-9L background challenge test sets.
rows.note: CT improves original and mixed-rand accuracy and is equal on mixed-same.
rows.check: Background-challenge test accuracy is a method-performance comparison and cannot establish any listed optimization effect.

rows.subject: ResNet-50 with CT
rows.operation_detail: Compared background gap, defined as mixed-same minus mixed-rand accuracy.
rows.note: Authors say CT reduces the overall gap.
rows.check: The background gap measures sensitivity to background cues, not an optimization effect. This is a derived summary of R17, not an independent experiment.
